Using references

Your colleagues will probably add citations in Word with Zotero, and they’ll want to see them in a normal style such as APA or Vancouver, not as Pandoc citation keys. This article shows how to bring Zotero citations from Word into Markdown, and how to send a document back to Word with the citations still live, so they can carry on editing them in Zotero.

You need Zotero and its Better BibTeX add-on.

From Word to Markdown

Before converting the document, swap its citations for citation keys and export a bibliography:

  1. Open the document in Word. Save a copy first if you want to keep the linked citations, although knittogether can give you working citations back later.
  2. On the Zotero tab, click Document Preferences, choose the citation style “Better BibTeX Citekeys” and click OK.
  3. Still on the Zotero tab, click Unlink Citations and accept the warning. Each citation is now plain text such as [@roseRosesStrategyPreventive2008], which Pandoc understands.
  4. In Zotero, right-click the collection that holds the references, choose Export Collection, pick Better BibTeX as the format and save the .bib file in your project.

It’s easiest if each project has its own Zotero collection, so the bibliography holds only the references you use.

Then convert and clean as usual, with clean_citations = TRUE (see vignette("knittogether")), and list the .bib file under bibliography in your Quarto document.

From Markdown back to Word, with live citations

To give your colleague a Word document where the citations still work in Zotero, you need three files:

  • The .bib file you exported above.
  • A citation style (.csl), for example from the Citation Style Language styles repository.
  • zotero.lua, a Lua filter from Better BibTeX that turns citation keys back into live Zotero citations.

Add them to the YAML of your .qmd:

format:
  docx: default
csl: elsevier-vancouver.csl
bibliography: example.bib
filters:
  - zotero.lua

Zotero needs to be running when you render. You can then go round as often as you like: Word to Markdown to Word, with live references each time. Just remember to unlink the citations (steps 2 and 3 above) each time before converting.

If something goes wrong

  • Citations show up with backslashes, such as \[@key\]. Converting to a different Markdown flavour, for example with convert_markdown(pandoc_args = "--to=markdown_strict"), can add extra escaping. Run clean_markdown(clean_citations = TRUE) to remove it.
  • A citation doesn’t link to its reference. The key in the document doesn’t match the key in the .bib file. In Zotero, check or edit the item’s citation key so the two agree, then export the bibliography again.

vignette("extended-workflow") includes a document with a citation you can try this on.
